newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end higher, off peaks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end higher, off peaks.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended pit trading higher but well off session peaks as traders braced for retail-level inflation figures on Friday.
August's consumer price index is forecast on average rising 0.2 percent overall and in the core rate.
Retail sales are seen gaining 0.7 percent and rising 0.4 percent without autos.
After Thursday's tame producer price index, which rose 0.3 percent with the core rate off 0.1 percent, traders wondered whether the benign tone would extend to the consumer-level report as well.

December Treasury bond futures popped up to the session's high before midday, supported by technical buying after the contract spiked up early to 107-11/32 on decent volume and showed few signs of backing off again.
After struggling with resistance at the one-week high of 107-13/32, the contract jumped up to touch 107-18/32, where buying stalled out, traders said.
Some traders had expected the contract to challenge the two-week peak at 107-22/32, but dealer and big local long liquidation cropped up and smacked it down again.

Some T-bond and Eurodollar traders traced the influx of liquidation to a Reuters story saying a Federal Reserve source said some Federal Open Market Committee members are concerned about a milder than expected second-half slowdown but that the consensus is that any inflation acceleration will be gradual.
"We turned on a dime," a T-bond futures floor broker said of the reaction to the story.
Futures then carved out ranges for the day's balance as activity slowed significantly.
"We were bored the last couple hours," said a Eurodollar floor broker. "The pit just seemed to die."

At settlement, December T-bonds rose 15/32 to 107-08/32, T-notes gained 11/32 to 106-03/32, munis rose 11/32 to 112-02/32, Eurodollars rose five bps to 93.99, and T-bills added five bps to 94.59. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
